lab_title: Anatomy and Circulation of the Human Heart
top_level_objectives: Identify and locate the four chambers of the human heart.
Identify and locate the four major valves of the human heart.
Identify and locate the major blood vessels connected to the human heart.
Trace the path of deoxygenated and oxygenated blood through the heart's dual-loop circulation.
Explain the functional significance of the heart's structure, including the role of valves and myocardial thickness.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the external structures of the human heart, orienting the student to its overall form and major visible vessels.
key_visuals: A realistic 3D model of the human heart, showing the exterior.
Labels for the aorta, pulmonary artery, superior and inferior vena cava.
A visual indicator highlighting the general location of the four chambers beneath the surface.
student_actions: Rotate the heart model to view it from all angles.
Tap on labels to identify the superior and inferior vena cava, aorta, and pulmonary artery.
Observe the relative positions of these major vessels.

scenes.brief_purpose: Reveal the internal structure of the heart, focusing on the identification of the four chambers.
key_visuals: The heart model with a section removed or made transparent to show the internal cavities.
Clear labels for the right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium, and left ventricle.
Color-coding to differentiate the right and left sides.
student_actions: Identify and tap on each of the four chambers.
Observe the relative sizes of the chambers, noting the larger size of the ventricles.
Compare the thickness of the myocardial walls between the right and left ventricles.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the four major heart valves and their locations within the heart.
key_visuals: The heart model with internal structures visible.
Highlighted 3D models of the tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral (bicuspid), and aortic valves.
Labels for each valve.
Animated visual cues showing valve leaflets opening and closing.
student_actions: Locate and tap on each of the four valves.
Observe the position of each valve relative to the chambers and major vessels.
Watch the valve animations to understand their function in preventing backflow.

scenes.brief_purpose: Trace the path of deoxygenated blood from the body, through the right side of the heart, to the lungs.
key_visuals: The heart model with chambers and valves visible.
An animated flow of blue particles representing deoxygenated blood.
Arrows indicating the path: Vena Cava -> Right Atrium -> Tricuspid Valve -> Right Ventricle -> Pulmonary Valve -> Pulmonary Artery.
student_actions: Follow the animated blue particles as they move through the right side of the heart.
Identify the structures the deoxygenated blood passes through in sequence.
Confirm the closure of the mitral valve during this phase.

scenes.brief_purpose: Trace the path of oxygenated blood from the lungs, through the left side of the heart, to the rest of the body.
key_visuals: The heart model with chambers and valves visible.
An animated flow of red particles representing oxygenated blood.
Arrows indicating the path: Pulmonary Veins -> Left Atrium -> Mitral Valve -> Left Ventricle -> Aortic Valve -> Aorta.
student_actions: Follow the animated red particles as they move through the left side of the heart.
Identify the structures the oxygenated blood passes through in sequence.
Confirm the closure of the pulmonary valve during this phase.
Note the thicker wall of the left ventricle compared to the right ventricle.

scenes.brief_purpose: Integrate the understanding of both pulmonary and systemic circulation by simulating a complete cardiac cycle.
key_visuals: The heart model showing all internal structures.
Simultaneous animation of both blue (deoxygenated) and red (oxygenated) blood flow.
Synchronized animations of all four valves opening and closing.
Visual representation of atrial and ventricular contraction.
student_actions: Observe the entire cardiac cycle, tracking both blood flows concurrently.
Correlate the timing of valve actions with the contraction of the chambers.
Reinforce the understanding of the heart's role as a dual pump.
